To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel bone targeting nanoparticle (BTNPs) was developed for the treatment of bone metastasis, and the BTNP was optimized for systemic circulation time and bone targeting to improve bone tumor treatment efficacy.

a bone targeting nanoparticle formulation of the GANT58 small molecule inhibitor of Gli2, which drives PTHrP expression, can inhibit tumor-associated bone destruction in a breast cancer bone metastatic mouse model.
the bone-targeted Gli2 inhibitor nanoparticles developed in this study have the potential to be used to treat bone metastases in patients with breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a targeted nanoparticulate drug delivery system to deliver GANT58 to bone-associated tumors and to inhibit tumor-induced bone destruction in breast cancer patients.
the development of a targeted nanoparticle formulation that can be used to deliver Gli2-inhibition to the tumor-bone microenvironment to prevent bone destruction.
the design of targeted nanotherapeutics for the treatment of metastatic bone disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GANT58-PPS-P(Aln-20-co-DMA) formulation is the best of the formulations tested and has the potential for clinical translation.

the Aln functionalized diblock copolymeric nanoparticles (BTNPs) can effectively inhibit the tumor induced osteoclast activation in bone metastasis model, and the Aln in BTNPs can provide dual benefit of targeting and direct antiresorptivity.
we have successfully developed a bone-targeted formulation that can deliver a small molecule inhibitor of a key transcription factor in bone-associated tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a bone-targeting nanocarrier that can be loaded with GANT58, a Gli2-inhibition drug.

we designed and optimized a targeted nanoplatform for bone metastasis treatment, and that this platform is capable of simultaneously delivering two different therapeutic modalities, a small molecule GANT58 inhibitor of the Hedgehog pathway, and a bisphosphonates for direct antiresorptivity.
we developed an effective targeted nanomedicine to treat bone metastasis by combining the bone-targeting ability of alendronate with the antitumor effect of a small molecule GANT58.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the balance of targeting and pharmacokinetics can be tuned by adjusting the ligand density on nanoparticles, which can be used to optimize the therapeutic outcomes for a variety of targeted nanotherapeutics.
we can use a combination of active and passive targeting to deliver therapeutics to bone metastatic lesions.
by tuning ligand density in the polymer block, we were able to optimize the systemic pharmacokinetics of the BTNP and increase bone:liver biodistributions ratio.
